description.narrative: In December 2021, the government, in consultation with the social partners, adopted an action plan to support a just transition. A Skills roadmap for green transition and advancing human capacity capital in Mauritius was developed and provided an action plan for the country. Under the UN Joint Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE), the ILO supported the drafting of the initial working version of the Skills Roadmap and organized an online workshop with key stakeholders involved in skills development and policy making in Mauritius. The process started in September 2021 and ended in December 2021 with the validation workshop.

description.narrative:
The government through the National Productivity and Competitiveness Council (NPCC) operationalized a programme promoting productivity at sectoral level, fostering training on innovation and business management for within-enterprises productivity improvements. In this regard:
1- As at November 2020, ten enterprises, participating in the Sustaining Competitive and Responsible Enterprises (SCORE) programme, benefited from the Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) COVID-19 training of trainers and enabled enterprises to adopt new safety and sanitation protocols arising from the COVID-19.
2- On August 2021, the NPCC signed a MOU and a Statement of Work with the Ministry of Tourism mandating NPCC to roll SCORE Covid-19 OSH training to the tourism and hospitality sector in a first phase and subsequently roll out SCORE Resource Efficiency Training "Operation COSHARE" to the sector in a 2nd phase Under the UN Joint Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) the ILO : 1- Conducted an on-line training session during the lockdown period (9 to 11 November 2020) on SCORE Module 5 on Occupational Safety and Health, which was adapted to address Covid-19 in order to ensure that enterprises implement Covid-19 safety protocols in the work place. The ILO capacitated trainers from NPCC, both certified SCORE trainers and new trainers, to roll out the SCORE Covid-19 OSH training to enterprises that had already gone through SCORE as well as to additional enterprises. 2- As a result of the training and intense joint efforts by NPCC and the ILO to share the positive results, NPCC was subsequently mandated by the Government of Mauritius to roll out the SCORE Covid-19 OSH training to the entire enterprise population of Mauritius in order to prepare for the re-opening of borders for international tourism as well as to make enterprises more resource efficient. The programme "COVID-19 OSH & Resource Efficiency" was branded by the ILO as "Operation COSHARE" and the ILO is contributing financially to the contract of an international SCORE expert to oversee the process as well as sharing some of the costs for NPCC to organise all the logistics and the preparation, roll out and monitoring of Operation COSHARE.
With a view to compensate tha lack of certified SCORE Trainers to implement Operation COSHARE, it was proposed to tap into the pool of unemployed OSH graduates in order to train them accordingly so as to allow them to benefit from the governmental schemes under the Human Resource Development Council (HRDC) and NPCC.
